prerequisites: Knowledge of dynamical systems and automatic control (Automatic Control exam)

learning_outcomes.text: By the end of the course, students will know and understand the models and control principles of mobile robotic systems, with reference to quadrotors, as well as the main methodologies for motion planning, state estimation, localization, mapping, vision, and learning.

Students will be able to formulate basic models, set up control and stabilization problems, select planning and filtering algorithms, and interpret the use of the studied techniques in mobile robotics scenarios.

Students will be able to critically evaluate the suitability of models, control algorithms, planning algorithms, and estimation methods with respect to the requirements of an application, recognizing assumptions, limitations, and main trade-offs.
Students will be able to describe problems, models, and solutions for mobile robots using appropriate technical language and presenting their reasoning clearly.
Students will develop autonomous learning skills that allow them to further study advanced mobile robotics techniques and to use specialized teaching and bibliographic material.

syllabus_topics: Feedback control: linearization
Lyapunov asymptotic stability
Hovering control
Trajectory stabilization
Linear quadratic regulator (LQR)
Motion planning in environments with obstacles: discrete search techniques (breadth-first search and depth-first search)
Discrete optimal planning (Dijkstra and A* algorithms)
Randomized techniques (Rapid Random Tree, Rapid Random Graph, and RRT*)
Continuous trajectory planning
Differential flatness
State estimation, localization, mapping, and SLAM: nondeterministic filters and the Bayesian filter
Kalman filter, extended Kalman filter, and particle filter
Localization with a known map
Mapping with known robot pose
SLAM (Simultaneous Localization and Mapping)
Radio Frequency Localization Systems
Vision and learning for robotics: introduction to vision
Optical flow for reconstructing object velocity in the image plane
Principles of deep learning for image processing (stochastic gradient descent, multilayer perceptron, backpropagation, overfitting and regularization, convolutional neural networks)
Introductory notions of reinforcement learning for robot control
Overview of the ethical, social, and economic impacts of robotics
Legal issues and challenges arising from the deployment of robotic systems
assessment_rules: The final examination consists of a written test followed by an oral discussion. The written test and the final grade (which takes into account both the written test and the oral discussion) are each graded on a 30-point scale. Incoming international exchange students may arrange to take the examination in English.
